subject: Interviewer lifeboat & skill-match plan — Q2 candidate surge
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ruth Park <ruth.park@external-recruiter.com>
Date: 2027-05-22T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Interviewer lifeboat idea for next week's slate

Hey team,

We're expecting a denser candidate slate next week (several late-stage SWE screens). I'd like to propose a short "lifeboat" pool: 3-4 cross-functional interviewers who can step in last-minute for coverage and help match specialty gaps (frontend, systems, infra). High-level asks:

- Volunteers who can cover up to 2 emergency swaps per week
- Explicit skill tags (frontend, infra, ML infra, product sense)
- Availability windows (PST) for quick scheduling

Can each of you reply with: 1) whether you can volunteer, 2) your skill tags, and 3) blackout times? I can coordinate with recruiting (Ruth) to only use the pool when primary panelists are unavailable.

Quick note: try to avoid volunteers who are on deep project launches (we'll need steady coverage).

Thanks,
Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Sr. Engineering Manager, Recruiting Partnerships
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Date: 2027-05-22T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Interviewer lifeboat idea for next week's slate

Hey Lauren — thanks for kicking this off. TL;DR: I support the lifeboat pool, and below are constraints I want tracked in the roster:

- Don’t use lifeboat for hire-sensitive debriefs (no replacements for hiring manager panels)
- Prioritize skill-match over title-match — e.g., a strong infra interviewer > random senior SWE
- Max 2 swaps per interviewer per rolling week; track in roster spreadsheet

I'll add a quick skill matrix template (simple CSV) to the roster Monica will compile. Recruiting: please only ping the pool after two scheduling attempts with the primary panelist.

Thanks — I'll also flag folks who are on-call this quarter so we don't overload them.

Marissa
Marissa Cole
